To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA sequences flanking the silk fibro in gene of Bombyx mor i contain a large number of repeated elements, and that a single repeated sequence element, called Bm-1, can be identified in the DNA from all Bombyx species examined.
repeated DNA sequences are found near the fibroin genes and are not associated with transcription of these genes.

repeated DNA sequences are found in the DNA flanking a developmentally regulated gene and that these repeated sequences are interspersed with single-copy sequences in the genome of the silkworm, Bombyx morii.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular organization of the silk fibromin gene in the silkworm, Bombyx morii.
the organization of repeated sequences in a eukaryotic genome.
the structure and organization of repeated DNA sequences in the silk moth genome and their relationship to the fibroin structural gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 5'-flanking region of the silk gene is not unusual in the sense that the repeated sequences are not unique to the gene.
repeated sequences comprise an extremely large proportion of the Bombyx genome and that they are not randomly dispersed.
the repeated sequences are not associated with the silk fibroins gene and that the repeated sequences may be associated with the regulation of the fibroins gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 5' flanking DNA of the silk fiborin gene is a mosaic of repeated sequence elements and single-copy DNA, that the repeated elements are not organized into clusters, and that the repeated elements have been evolving in the genome by a mechanism of sequence divergence.
the silk fibroins of the Bombyx are encoded by a family of closely related genes, each of which is preceded by a large region of repeated DNA.
repeated DNA sequences are not randomly dispersed but rather are organized in a nonrandom fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
repeated sequences are not confined to the DNA of transposable elements, satellite DNA, or the 5'-ends of genes.
the 5' region of the fibroins gene is a single copy gene and that the repeated sequence elements are located in the 3' region of the gene.
there is no simple pattern in the distribution of repetitive sequences around the fibroin locus.
